preamble: Shift of the bilabial fricative [ɸ] to the labiodental fricative [f]. The clearest case is Germanic: the Proto-Germanic reflex of PIE *p (Grimm's law) was probably still a bilabial [ɸ], written *f, which became labiodental [f] in the daughter languages. A bilabial stage between Greek [pʰ] and [f] for φ has been proposed but lacks specific evidence, so Greek is not listed here.

examples.note: Proto-Germanic *f was probably still realized as bilabial [ɸ] (Gothic final devoicing of b to f and Old Norse spellings such as aptr point to a bilabial value); the daughter languages have labiodental [f].
